import pickle
from datetime import date, timedelta

# day-of-year by month/day, leap-year calendar (1 Jan=1 ... 31 Dec=366, 29 Feb=60)
leap_cum = [0,31,60,91,121,152,182,213,244,274,305,335]
def doy(d):
    return leap_cum[d.month-1] + d.day
# sanity checks
assert doy(date(2017,1,1))==1
assert doy(date(2017,2,28))==59
assert doy(date(2000,2,29))==60
assert doy(date(2017,3,1))==61
assert doy(date(2017,12,30))==365
assert doy(date(2017,12,31))==366
assert doy(date(2016,12,31))==366  # non-leap Dec 31 still 366 by (month,day) mapping

d0 = date(1991,12,27); d1 = date(2003,1,5)
dates = []
cur = d0
while cur <= d1:
    dates.append(cur); cur += timedelta(days=1)
print("n dates:", len(dates))
dpos = {d:i for i,d in enumerate(dates)}

b0 = date(1992,1,1); b1 = date(2002,12,31)
pools = {}
cur = b0
while cur <= b1:
    dd = doy(cur)
    if dd != 60:
        idxs = pools.setdefault(dd, [])
        for k in range(-5,6):
            t = cur + timedelta(days=k)
            assert d0 <= t <= d1
            idxs.append(dpos[t])
    cur += timedelta(days=1)

print("n pool days:", len(pools))
bad = {d:len(v) for d,v in pools.items() if len(v)!=121 or len(set(v))!=121}
print("pools without exactly 121 distinct dates:", bad)
# examples
print("d=1 first/last:", dates[pools[1][0]], dates[pools[1][-1]])
print("d=366 first/last:", dates[pools[366][0]], dates[pools[366][-1]])
print("d=59 first/last:", dates[pools[59][0]], dates[pools[59][-1]])
print("d=61 first/last:", dates[pools[61][0]], dates[pools[61][-1]])
# check 29 Feb values appear in neighbour pools (d=59 and d=61 of leap years)
feb29 = date(1996,2,29)
for dd in (59,60,61):
    if dd in pools:
        print("feb29 1996 in pool d=%d:" % dd, dpos[feb29] in pools[dd])
pickle.dump({"dates":dates, "pools":pools}, open("/tmp/pools.pkl","wb"))
print("saved /tmp/pools.pkl")

import numpy as np, pickle, time
X = np.load("/tmp/X.npy")
pools = pickle.load(open("/tmp/pools.pkl","rb"))["pools"]
meta = pickle.load(open("/tmp/target.pkl","rb"))
sea = meta["sea"]
Nc = 3600
Xd = X.reshape(4028, Nc)

thr = np.full((366, Nc), np.nan)
clim = np.full((366, Nc), np.nan)
t0=time.time()
import warnings
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
    for d in range(1, 367):
        if d == 60:
            continue
        pool = Xd[pools[d]]                      # (121, 3600)
        thr[d] = np.nanquantile(pool, 0.9, method="hazen", axis=0)
        clim[d] = np.nanmean(pool, axis=0)
print("pools done in", round(time.time()-t0,1), "s")

# day-60 fill (before smoothing)
thr[60] = 0.5*(thr[59] + thr[61])
clim[60] = 0.5*(clim[59] + clim[61])

# unweighted centred 31-day moving mean, wrap-around over 366 days
def smooth31(a):
    a2 = np.concatenate([a, a, a])              # (1098, Nc)
    # day index d (1..366) -> 0-based d-1; window d-15..d+15 mod 366 -> start (d-1-15)+366
    starts = np.arange(366) - 15 + 366          # 0-based start in a2 for each d
    out = np.empty_like(a)
    for d in range(366):
        out[d] = a2[starts[d]:starts[d]+31].mean(axis=0)
    return out
t0=time.time()
thr_s = smooth31(thr)
clim_s = smooth31(clim)
print("smoothing done in", round(time.time()-t0,1), "s")
print("thr range:", np.nanmin(thr_s), np.nanmax(thr_s), "clim range:", np.nanmin(clim_s), np.nanmax(clim_s))
print("any NaN thr at sea cells:", np.isnan(thr_s).any(axis=0)[sea].any(),
      "| any NaN clim at sea cells:", np.isnan(clim_s).any(axis=0)[sea].any())
pickle.dump({"thr_s":thr_s, "clim_s":clim_s}, open("/tmp/thrclim.pkl","wb"))
print("saved /tmp/thrclim.pkl")

import numpy as np, pickle, time
X = np.load("/tmp/X.npy")
pools = pickle.load(open("/tmp/pools.pkl","rb"))["pools"]
Nc = 3600
Xd = X.reshape(4028, Nc)

def hazen90(pool):
    # pool: (121, Nc) float64, may contain NaN
    S = np.sort(pool, axis=0)                      # NaNs sort last
    nv = 121 - np.isnan(pool).sum(axis=0)          # valid counts (Nc,)
    j = 0.9*nv - 0.5                               # 0-based virtual index (HF type 5: h1 = 0.9*nv+0.5)
    jf = np.floor(j).astype(np.int64)
    jc = np.minimum(jf+1, 120)
    # clamp jf to [0,120]; for nv==0 jf=-1 -> maps to NaN slot (last is NaN)
    jf = np.clip(jf, 0, 120)
    frac = j - jf
    a = np.take_along_axis(S, jf[None,:], axis=0)[0]
    b = np.take_along_axis(S, jc[None,:], axis=0)[0]
    val = a + frac*(b-a)
    val = np.where(nv > 0, val, np.nan)
    return val

# cross-validate vs numpy nanquantile on random pools
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
ok = True
for trial in range(30):
    p = rng.normal(285, 2, (121, 50)).astype("float64")
    m = rng.random((121,50)) < rng.uniform(0, 0.5)
    p[m] = np.nan
    ref = np.array([np.nanquantile(p[:,k], 0.9, method="hazen") for k in range(50)])
    got = hazen90(p)
    if not np.allclose(ref, got, equal_nan=True, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12):
        ok = False
        print("MISMATCH", trial, ref[:5], got[:5])
        break
print("cross-validation:", "PASS" if ok else "FAIL")

def cell_mhw(h):
    # h: (nt,) bool -> merged MHW mask (nt,)
    m = np.zeros_like(h)
    if not h.any():
        return m
    idx = np.flatnonzero(h)
    # split into runs
    breaks = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(idx) > 1)
    starts = np.concatenate([[idx[0]], idx[breaks+1]])
    ends   = np.concatenate([idx[breaks], [idx[-1]]])
    runs = [(s,e) for s,e in zip(starts, ends) if e-s+1 >= 5]
    # one-pass merge of gaps <= 2
    merged = []
    for s,e in runs:
        if merged and s - merged[-1][1] - 1 <= 2:
            merged[-1][1] = e
        else:
            merged.append([s,e])
    for s,e in merged:
        m[s:e+1] = True
    return m

import numpy as np

def cell_mhw(h):
    m = np.zeros_like(h, bool)
    if not h.any():
        return m
    idx = np.flatnonzero(h)
    breaks = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(idx) > 1)
    starts = np.concatenate([[idx[0]], idx[breaks+1]])
    ends   = np.concatenate([idx[breaks], [idx[-1]]])
    runs = [(s,e) for s,e in zip(starts, ends) if e-s+1 >= 5]
    merged = []
    for s,e in runs:
        if merged and s - merged[-1][1] - 1 <= 2:
            merged[-1][1] = e
        else:
            merged.append([s,e])
    for s,e in merged:
        m[s:e+1] = True
    return m

# reference implementation: explicit intervals with iterative merging
def ref_mhw(h):
    idx = np.flatnonzero(h)
    runs = []
    if len(idx):
        s = idx[0]; p = idx[0]
        for i in idx[1:]:
            if i == p+1: p = i
            else: runs.append([s,p]); s = i; p = i
        runs.append([s,p])
    runs = [r for r in runs if r[1]-r[0]+1 >= 5]
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        new = [runs[0]]
        for r in runs[1:]:
            if r[0] - new[-1][1] - 1 <= 2:
                new[-1][1] = r[1]; changed = True
            else:
                new.append(r)
        runs = new
    m = np.zeros_like(h, bool)
    for s,e in runs: m[s:e+1] = True
    return m

assert len(dates) == 92

def cell_mhw(h):
    m = np.zeros_like(h, bool)
    if not h.any():
        return m
    idx = np.flatnonzero(h)

Tf = T.reshape(92, 3600)
sea_flat = sea.reshape(3600)
hot = Tf >= thr_s[doys]                       # NaN SST -> False
M = np.zeros((92, 3600), dtype=np.uint8)
n_mhw_cells = 0
for c in np.flatnonzero(sea_flat):
    if hot[:, c].any():
        m = cell_mhw(hot[:, c])
        M[:, c] = m.astype(np.uint8)
        if m.any():
            n_mhw_cells += 1

events = []
i = 0
while i < 92:
    if active[i]:
        j = i
        while j+1 < 92 and active[j+1]: j += 1
        events.append({"onset": dates[i].isoformat(), "end": dates[j].isoformat()})
        i = j+1
    else:
        i += 1
